source_text: Sed iam pergamus ad reliqua. Postquam ergo Abrahae, quod a me positum fuerat, vitavit exemplum; conatus est asserere, Abimelech quoque, qui orante Abraham ba, cum mulieribus suis sanatus, refertur, ut ad generationis operam, a qua per plagam erat suspensus, posset redire, non detractione libidinis, sed dolore aliquo posse intellegi mulierum vulvam fuisse conclusam [n35] ; quasi a nobis assereretur impendio, ut appetitus eis naturalis redditus videretur; cum ego testimoniis illis id solum probare fuerim contentus, impeditum concubitum, qui sine libidine esse non poterat, per iram Dei, redditumque per indulgentiam Dei, sive amolitis obstaculis, sive irritamentis sollemnibus restitutis; tamen diabolicum non doceri, sed etiam per hoc ad Dei operam pertinentem, qui inter corporis instrumenta mediocria, sed innoxia, non specie, non modo, verum solo peccaret excessu.
pass_a_gloss: But now let us proceed to the rest. After therefore he avoided Abraham's example, which had been set down by me; he tried to assert that Abimelech also, who with Abraham praying is reported healed with his women, so that he could return to the work of generation from which he had been hung by a plague, can be understood not by a taking-away of lust but by some pain that the women's womb was closed; as if it were being asserted by us with expense that a natural appetite seemed restored to them; when I was content to prove by those testimonies only that intercourse, which could not be without lust, was impeded through God's wrath, and restored through God's indulgence, whether obstacles having been removed or solemn irritants restored; nevertheless it is not taught diabolical, but even through this belonging to God's work, who among the body's middling but harmless instruments would sin not by species, not by measure, but by excess alone.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: But let us proceed to what remains. After avoiding Abraham’s example, which I had put forward, he tried to maintain the following about Abimelech. Abimelech is reported to have been healed with his women when Abraham prayed, so that he could return to the work of generation from which a plague had suspended him (Genesis 20:17–18). Augustine says the closing of the women’s wombs may be understood as some pain, rather than removal of sexual desire (Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.15.30). As though we were urgently insisting that their natural appetite must appear restored! In those testimonies I was content to prove only this: intercourse, which could not occur without sexual desire, was prevented through God’s anger and restored through God’s mercy, whether by obstacles being removed or by the usual stimuli being restored. It is therefore not shown diabolical, but by this very fact belongs to God’s activity. Among the body’s functions it is an ordinary but innocent instrument, wrong not in its kind or proper measure, but only in excess.

choices.why: Julian's pudenda libido is the appetite accompanying union, not a created substance of sin.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
